shots.why: first participant, intact: a woman laying a table in a 1940 film. Thirteen seconds of one job, no cutting.
second participant, whoever raises this blind in Berlin; never seen. Silent source, room sound carried over from the table so the seam is audible as a borrowing.
shots.caption: Berlin, undated in this archive

shots.why: third: a woman at a sink, 1958, from a staged film whose husband is not listening. Keeps its fictional voice; fiction stays fiction.
shots.caption: 1958, a staged film

shots.why: handoff on water: sink to river, Modesta, undated in the archive. Women washing together, not one woman alone: the bigger frame already changes the job.
shots.caption: Modesta, undated

shots.why: continued, close: one woman at a stone, 1920, Dutch colonial footage. Silent source; the Modesta river is laid under it and the ledger says so.
shots.caption: 1920, Dutch colonial footage

shots.why: widen: a whole channel of washers, in a street, filmed by someone from elsewhere. The handoff no longer reads as a continuation.
carrying: what the washers would do next, if this were a day, but it isn't.
carrying again, 1920. Stops before the camera's own close approach to a bare-chested woman at 9s, which the source film chose and this one declines.
the unfinished task. Back at the sink, she is still washing and still not being heard; the film leaves mid-sentence and never comes back.
return to the first film after its job: what she laid is now under a child's elbows. A different pace, and this film's own boast about pioneers, which the morning has not earned.
shots.caption:
This is not one morning.
Five films, made decades and continents apart, put in this order here.
